questions.question: Why is it more dangerous to drive at night than during the day?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because of darkness and headlight glare from other cars. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you move your car. You should also adjust your seat, fasten your seatbelt, and secure loose items. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign marks a crosswalk. Watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable. They may suddenly change direction without warning. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see, so stay alert.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Watch for people crossing your path.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.explanation: This orange sign warns that roadwork is coming. Pay attention to temporary traffic control devices in work zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down; curving road ahead.
Slow down and do not use your brakes.
Slow down; slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching the end of a divided highway.
You are approaching the beginning of a divided highway.
The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are approaching the beginning of a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is starting ahead. Stay to the right of the median divider.

questions.question: What does this sign tell a driver?

options.text: A construction flagger is ahead.
A police officer is ahead.
A parking attendant is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns of a flag person ahead. Follow their directions. Flaggers wear orange or yellow vests or bright jackets. They use paddles and red flags to direct traffic through work zones.

questions.question: Which of these is unlawful?

options.text: Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass on hills, curves, or where you cannot see far enough ahead. You cannot pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, where no passing signs are posted, where a solid yellow line is on your side, when a car has stopped for a pedestrian, or in work zones where it is unsafe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way.
No passing zone.
Reduction in lanes.

questions.explanation: A red and white triangle sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
Areas where cars have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Areas where cars are several car lengths away from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars vanish from the driver's view or are so close that they make it unsafe for the truck driver to stop or turn. A car in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars on the right move first.
You have the right-of-way.
Let cross traffic pass before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cross traffic pass before proceeding.
questions.explanation: This sign means you must yield the right-of-way. Slow down and let vehicles and pedestrians cross before you proceed. Stop if necessary.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. Turning right here would be unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times quickly.
Slow down gradually without braking hard.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking hard.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Take your foot off the gas and do not brake hard. Let the car slow down on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: The height from the road to a bridge or overpass.
The maximum legal height for vehicles in this state.
The maximum width for vehicles on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The height from the road to a bridge or overpass.
questions.explanation: This is a low clearance warning sign. It shows the distance from the road to the bottom of a bridge or overpass.

questions.question: When should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on a level roadway with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight ahead so a rear-end collision does not push you into oncoming traffic. On hills or slopes, turn your wheels so the car will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive with caution, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed on roads near schools to warn drivers to slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.question: What does a sign with this shape mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Warning.
Signal ahead.

questions.explanation: A diamond-shaped yellow sign warns you of possible danger ahead. Orange diamond signs warn of possible dangers in or near work areas.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and cars already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: If you become tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or change drivers if you become tired. Fatigue slows your reaction time and makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean you cannot pass from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.explanation: A round yellow sign means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving on the highway:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
Allows you to spot police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Looking ahead helps you avoid sudden braking or turning. You can drive safer, save fuel, and keep traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: The crossing is controlled. Continue at your normal speed.
Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Let trains pass before you cross.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. At what speed can this happen?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when there is standing water on the road. At 35 mph and below, most tires push water away. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move the water fast enough, and your car may slide on the water like water skis.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
The lane must turn right.
A right turn is allowed only with a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow or yellow-green. They tell you about road conditions ahead, such as curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must let you go first.
You must let the pedestrian go first.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let the pedestrian go first.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must yield the right-of-way to them.

questions.question: What does this orange triangle symbol mean?

options.text: Dangerous intersections ahead.
A slow-moving vehicle.
Yield sign.

questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it moves slowly. You may see it on farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn carriages. It looks orange during the day and red at night.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter.
Use only the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for cars in your blind spot. You may need to check multiple times. Also watch the traffic in front of you and next to you.

questions.question: Why do large trucks need extra space in front of them?

options.text: To let other drivers merge onto the freeway.
So the truck can stop safely.
To give other drivers room when they slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck can stop safely.
questions.explanation: Trucks take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then brake or stop suddenly.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, how long does it take for the alcohol effects to wear off?

options.text: A cold shower will reduce the effects.
Wait several hours.
Drinking coffee will reduce the effects.

questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. A cold shower, exercise, or coffee will not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: What does this speed limit sign mean?

options.text: You must drive 55 mph through the intersection.
The maximum speed is 55 mph under good conditions.
You must not drive slower than 55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed is 55 mph under good conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the highest speed allowed on this road. You can drive slower based on weather or road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 pounds are allowed.
A hill is ahead.
A truck stop is ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: You have a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a minor collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What is the correct way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Stay near the right curb, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay as close as possible to the right curb as you approach the turn.
